claim: In the original Chevalley-Serre algebra g_S(A(1,1)), for every integer k>=1, the entire formal root-degree space g_(k,k,k+1) is one-dimensional, lies in the positive level-(k+1) piece, and is killed by f1 and f2. The ordinary map ad(f3):g_(k,k,k+1)->g_(k,k,k) is injective and has one-dimensional image. Equivalently, the original finite-Levi adjoint-type (1,1) critical-lowest source in that degree has dimension one and its f3 kernel is zero. At level five the specialization k=4 is the ORIGINAL degree (4,4,5), type 8, and both original obstruction multiplicities and the same-type migration T multiplicity vanish there. This says nothing about the full type-8 parameter family or any other type.
reflection_setup: For i=1,2,3, the operators ad(e_i) and ad(f_i) are locally nilpotent on the original algebra: each is nilpotent on every Chevalley generator by the defining positive/negative Serre and Chevalley relations, and the derivation rule extends this to finite Lie words. Hence the finite-on-each-vector exponentials tau_i=exp(ad e_i) exp(-ad f_i) exp(ad e_i) are automorphisms. The elementary sl2 Weyl identity makes tau_i send the FORMAL root component g_gamma bijectively to g_(s_i gamma). This remains a statement in the Z^3 grading even though this particular Cartan matrix is singular: the exponentials change only the i-th root coefficient and reverse the h_i eigenvalue, fixing its reflected coefficient uniquely.
For A(1,1), the reflections act on (a,b,n) by s1(a,b,n)=(b+n-a,b,n), s2(a,b,n)=(a,a+n-b,n), s3(a,b,n)=(a,b,a+b-n). These are the direct Chevalley weight formulas, not an enumerated root table.

The adopted actual parabolic decomposition is Splus direct-sum g0 direct-sum Sminus. In its formal simple-root grading, positive pieces have all coefficients nonnegative, negative pieces all nonpositive, and g0 has only the finite-Levi roots and degree zero. Thus every mixed-sign formal component is zero. The simple root spaces of e3 and e2 are each one-dimensional: respectively the lowest line of the actual adjoint V and the corresponding finite-sl3 root line.
proof_of_entire_source_and_lowestness: Write alpha_k=(k,k,k+1). For k>=2, successive reflections s3, s1, s2, s1 give (k,k,k-1), (k-1,k,k-1), (k-1,k-2,k-1), (k-2,k-2,k-1)=alpha_(k-2). The base alpha_0=(0,0,1) is the e3 simple root; for alpha_1=(1,1,2), s3 then s1 gives (1,1,0) then (0,1,0), the e2 simple root. Therefore every g_alpha_k is isomorphic, via actual automorphisms, to one of these one-dimensional simple-root spaces. This proves both nonzero source and exact dimension one, without a character or loop-model assumption.

Let beta_k=alpha_k-alpha_1=(k-1,k,k+1). For k>=3, successive s3,s2,s1 send beta_k to (k-1,k,k-2), then (k-1,k-3,k-2), then (k-4,k-3,k-2)=beta_(k-3). The remaining symbolic base classes vanish: beta_0=(-1,0,1) is mixed-sign; s3 beta_1=(0,1,-1) is mixed-sign; and s2 s3 beta_2=(1,-1,0) is mixed-sign. Since the reflection maps are isomorphisms, g_beta_k=0 for all k>=0. Hence [f1,g_alpha_k]=0.

Interchanging the labels 1 and 2 in the same symmetric A(1,1) root-lattice argument gives g_(alpha_k-alpha_2)=0 and [f2,g_alpha_k]=0. Thus the entire one-dimensional root space, not merely the image of a special representative, is finite-Levi-lowest.

The h3-weight of alpha_k is 2(k+1)-k-k=2. The positive-weight root-sl2 lemma therefore makes ad(f3) injective on this entire root space. For k>=1 its bracket has positive level k and is in the actual positive quotient, not an auxiliary Cartan target. Its image has dimension one because its source does. The finite-Levi lowest weights are (-1,-1), so the corresponding highest type is (1,1), the adjoint/type 8.
